record.paper_title: Neutrino theory: open questions and future opportunities
record.context_brief: Whether neutrino mass implies a new scale
record.original_question: Does the tiny neutrino mass scale point to a genuinely new physical mass scale beyond the known Standard Model scales, or can it instead be explained using already known scales together with extremely small dimensionless parameters such as neutrino Yukawa couplings of order 10^-12 or smaller?

evidence.quote: But now we should ask if the origin of the tiny neutrino mass scale relies on a genuinely new physical mass scale, or is instead derived from a known scale (or known scales) via tiny dimensionless parameters?

For example, if neutrino masses are generated in exactly the same way as the charged fermions in the SM, then they are equal to the Higgs vacuum expectation value (VEV) multiplied by tiny Yukawa coupling constants of order 10−12 or less.

artifact.self_contained_problem: In the Standard Model of particle physics, charged fermion masses arise from Yukawa couplings y_f to the Higgs field, whose vacuum expectation value is v ≈ 174 GeV, so that m_f = y_f v. Observed neutrino masses are constrained to be at most of order 0.1 eV, which would correspond to Dirac Yukawa couplings of order 10^(-12) or smaller if generated by the same Higgs mechanism. Alternatively, neutrino masses may be generated by mechanisms involving a new physical mass scale Λ distinct from the electroweak scale and the Planck scale (for instance, a seesaw scale associated with heavy right-handed neutrinos, leading to m_ν ~ v^2/Λ).\n\nDetermine whether the smallness of the observed neutrino mass scale necessarily implies the existence of a genuinely new physical mass scale beyond the known Standard Model scales (such as the electroweak scale and the Planck scale), or whether it can instead be accounted for using only the known scales together with extremely small dimensionless parameters such as Yukawa couplings of order 10^(-12) or less. Identify experimental or theoretical criteria that could distinguish between these two possibilities.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether neutrino masses arise from a new high-energy scale (e.g., seesaw mechanisms) or from tiny Dirac Yukawa couplings at the electroweak scale remains an open foundational question in neutrino physics, with no experimental determination as of 2026. Reviews continue to list this as among the leading open problems in neutrino theory.
